primary_claim: A backtracking steering vector computed from base-model (Llama-3.1-8B) activations induces backtracking behavior in the corresponding RL-finetuned reasoning model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B) but not in the base model itself, suggesting reasoning fine-tuning repurposes a pre-existing latent representation rather than learning a wholly new one.

effect.metric: effect of backtracking steering vector on emission of backtracking tokens (e.g. 'Wait'), reasoning model vs base model, vs baselines
effect.value: backtracking steering vector induces emission of backtracking tokens in the reasoning model but not the base model, with a substantially greater effect than baselines (mean activations, random noise, magnitude increase, other reasoning-behavior vectors)

stated_future_work: Hope these results inspire further investigation into the mechanisms involved in CoT reasoning
limitations_stated: Still not sure what concept the steering vector represents, or whether there is a single monosemantic concept it represents
Investigation into whether the direction represents something abstract like 'uncertainty' was inconclusive
quote: We find a direction which is present both in base models and associated reasoning-finetuned models but induces backtracking only in reasoning models.
